headline: LinkedIn's AI slop button clicked by over 1 million users
summary: The professional networking platform's new feature allows users to flag AI-generated content, with over a million clicks since its July 30th launch.
details: LinkedIn's Chief Product Officer Hari Srinivasan revealed that more than one million users have clicked the "Seems like AI slop" button since its introduction on July 30th.
This feature, accessible via the three-dot menu on posts, was launched shortly after AI detection tools reported a significant percentage of LinkedIn's longform posts as AI-generated.
In conjunction with the new button, LinkedIn has enhanced its AI classifiers and removed an AI-powered post enhancement feature.
Srinivasan stated that these measures have led to a 40% reduction in views for content classified as "AI slop" within weeks.
The platform is also implementing a notification system to inform users when their posts are flagged as potentially AI-generated by other members.

LinkedIn's Chief Product Officer Hari Srinivasan revealed that more than one million users have clicked the "Seems like AI slop" button since its introduction on July 30th.

In conjunction with the new button, LinkedIn has enhanced its AI classifiers and removed an AI-powered post enhancement feature.

Srinivasan stated that these measures have led to a 40% reduction in views for content classified as "AI slop" within weeks.

The platform is also implementing a notification system to inform users when their posts are flagged as potentially AI-generated by other members.
